meaning: to work or study late into the night
literal_translation: estudar ou trabalhar até muito tarde da noite
example: She burned the midnight oil to finish her research project before the deadline.
origin: Comes from the days when lamps were lit with oil, so working late meant burning a lot of oil.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to waste money on expensive cooking oil
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with spending money or buying oil.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to cook dinner very late at night
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about working or studying late, not about cooking.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to fall asleep during a lesson
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes staying awake to work, not falling asleep.

explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' comes from the time when lamps burned oil, so working late meant using oil late at night. It means to work or study late into the night.
